solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Hard negotiation tactic succeeded in doing rather badly

indicators.note: something done badly is botched, so the letters before it come out in a muddled order
the abbreviation is placed inside the rearranged letters, as the word in says

blocks.note: S is the standard abbreviation for succeeded, as in genealogies
taken as written, eleven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Someone whose bargaining style has brought them success is, ironically, performing poorly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Succeeded in doing' reads as one phrase, but succeeded is just S dropped into the jumble of DOING RATHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Horse trading is shrewd, hard-nosed bargaining with give and take, named after the haggling of livestock dealers.

clue.text: Lease removed from particular sort of car

indicators.note: removed from tells us to take one word's letters out of a longer phrase

blocks.note: a particular, fussy person is hard to please
taken as written

explanation.surface: A rental agreement has been taken off a specific kind of car.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is that 'particular' must be expanded to a whole phrase, HARD TO PLEASE, whose last five letters happen to spell LEASE.
explanation.definitionFit: A hardtop is a car with a rigid, fixed roof, as opposed to a convertible with a fabric one.

clue.text: Bird bones and bare dirt scattered alongside river

indicators.note: things scattered are thrown about at random, so these letters are rearranged
alongside means placed next to, so the river's letter simply sits beside the jumble

blocks.note: R is the usual abbreviation for river
taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A grim scene by a river bank: skeletal remains and exposed earth strewn about.
explanation.definitionFit: The robin redbreast is the full traditional name of the European robin, a common garden bird.

clue.text: Follow it out of bathroom, often?

indicators.note: out of means taken away from, so the short word is removed from the longer one

blocks.note: a bathroom attached to a bedroom is often an en suite, hence the question mark
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction to follow something out of the bathroom, as one does most mornings.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits that a bathroom is only sometimes en suite; take IT out of ENSUITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensue is to come after or result from something, which is what following means here.

clue.text: Old hutch hidden in tall grass is unlocked again

indicators.note: something hidden in another thing is tucked inside it, so these letters go within

blocks.note: a reed is a tall grass of wet ground
O is the standard abbreviation for old
a hutch or pen is an enclosure for animals

explanation.surface: An old rabbit hutch lost in long grass has been found and opened again.
explanation.definitionFit: Reopened means opened a second time, so a door unlocked again has been reopened.

clue.text: Heartfelt, extremely distinctive collection of songs

indicators.note: extremely points to the extremes of the next word, its first and last letters

blocks.note: the two end letters of the word
an EP, or extended play, is a short record of a few songs

explanation.surface: A music reviewer gushing about a truly original new release of songs.
explanation.definitionFit: Deep feelings are profound and sincere, which is what heartfelt describes.

clue.text: Hole flipping full of rats? Don't worry about it!

indicators.note: flipping something turns it over, so the word is read back to front
full of says the first word holds the second inside it

blocks.note: a den is a hollow or lair
rats are vermin

explanation.surface: Someone moans that their flipping hovel is overrun with rats, and is told not to fret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flipping' reads as a mild British curse but is the turn-round signal for the word for hole.
explanation.definitionFit: Never mind is the everyday phrase for telling someone to forget a matter and not be concerned.

clue.text: Machine enabling you to put your own pop into cans?

definitions.text: Machine enabling you to put your own pop into cans?

blocks.clueFragment: put your own pop into cans
blocks.note: surface reading: a home drinks-canning machine for fizzy soft drinks
setter's reading: cans is slang for headphones, and pop is the music you choose to play into them

explanation.surface: A gadget for canning your own home-made fizzy drink.
explanation.walkthrough: Pop and cans both suggest soft drinks; really they are pop music and headphones.
explanation.definitionFit: A personal stereo, like the Walkman, is a portable player that feeds your chosen music into headphones.

clue.text: A playwright read out On The Beach

indicators.note: something read out is spoken, so we want a word with the same sound as the name

blocks.note: taken as written
George Bernard Shaw, the Irish playwright, whose name sounds the same in a British accent

explanation.surface: A dramatist gives a reading of the novel On the Beach.
explanation.walkthrough: On The Beach looks like a title (Nevil Shute's novel), but it is the plain definition. SHAW and SHORE are said alike in non-rhotic British speech.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashore means on land by the water's edge, which is where someone on the beach is.

clue.text: Puzzle about what American restaurant staff may do

blocks.note: re means about or concerning

blocks.clueFragment: what American restaurant staff may do
blocks.note: in the US, to bus tables is to clear them, the job of a busboy

explanation.surface: A riddle concerning the duties of waiting staff in an American diner.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebus is a puzzle in which pictures or symbols stand for words or syllables.

clue.text: Surveys short public struggle with introduction of sanctions

indicators.note: short means cut off, so the word loses its last letter
the introduction of a word is its opening letter

blocks.note: overt means open, done in public
to vie is to compete or struggle
W is the abbreviation for with
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: Opinion polls report a brief public fight over the imposition of sanctions.
explanation.definitionFit: Overviews are general surveys of a subject, broad summaries rather than detailed studies.

clue.text: Cheeky kid given teddy occasionally played around

indicators.note: occasionally means every so often, so only every other letter is kept

blocks.note: a tinker is a mischievous child, an informal British usage
the second and fourth letters of the word

explanation.surface: A naughty child given a teddy bear played with it now and then.
explanation.definitionFit: To tinker is to fiddle or potter about with something, so tinkered means played around.

clue.text: At the end, pour in sauce quickly

indicators.note: at the end points to the final letter of the word that follows
in tells us to put that letter inside the next word

blocks.note: pesto is an Italian basil sauce
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A cooking instruction: finally, add the sauce fast.
explanation.definitionFit: Presto is the musical direction meaning very fast, and is used generally for quickly.

clue.text: Range covered by a minister

indicators.note: covered by means wrapped inside the following word

blocks.note: per means a, as in once per day
range and reach both mean extent

explanation.surface: A cooking range has been looked after by a clergyman.
explanation.walkthrough: Range suggests a kitchen stove or hills, but it is extent. The little word 'a' becomes PER, as in 'twice a week'.
explanation.definitionFit: A preacher is a minister of religion who delivers sermons.

clue.text: Spectre flying around that is frightening in the extreme

indicators.note: flying suggests the letters are sent all over the place and land in a new order
around means the jumble is wrapped round the next abbreviation

blocks.note: taken as written
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: A ghost flitting about is the scariest thing imaginable.
explanation.definitionFit: Creepiest is the superlative of creepy, so it means the most frightening or eerie.

clue.text: Couple drinking pub's Australian beer

indicators.note: drinking means taking in, so the first word swallows the second

blocks.note: to couple is to tie together
an inn is a pub; the 's stands for is, joining wordplay to definition

explanation.surface: A pair of drinkers at a bar enjoy a beer from Down Under.
explanation.definitionFit: A tinnie is Australian slang for a can of beer, from its tin container.

clue.text: Very productive expert has most of career in charge

indicators.note: most of means nearly all, so the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: a pro is a professional or expert
a career can be one's working life
IC is the abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A hardworking specialist who has run things for nearly all of their working life.
explanation.definitionFit: Prolific describes someone who produces a great deal of work, very productive.

clue.text: Trendy food lacking the first hint of anything natural

indicators.note: lacking means going without, so a letter is dropped from the food word
the first hint of a word is its initial letter

blocks.note: in means fashionable
bread is a staple food
the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fashionable health food without a trace of anything natural in it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Natural' looks like part of the food description; it is the definition, at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Inbred can mean inborn or innate, a quality that is natural to someone rather than learned.

clue.text: New, inexperienced journalist overwhelmed by two oppressive people

indicators.note: overwhelmed by means engulfed by, so these letters sit inside the next piece

blocks.note: II is two in Roman numerals
N is the abbreviation for new
a cub reporter is a novice journalist

explanation.surface: A green young reporter is bullied by a pair of tyrants.
explanation.definitionFit: Incubi are demons said to oppress sleepers, the source of the word's sense of a crushing burden or nightmare.

clue.text: Bakers can use these good sieves

blocks.note: G is the abbreviation for good
a riddle is a coarse sieve, as for soil or gravel

explanation.surface: Bakers are advised that these sieves are good for sifting flour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sieves' looks like the answer's meaning, but riddles is the wordplay word; bakers' griddles are flat cooking plates.
explanation.definitionFit: A griddle is a flat iron plate used for baking scones and oatcakes, so it is baking equipment.

clue.text: Operator certainly bored by nothing ultimately working

indicators.note: bored by means drilled into, so a letter is placed inside the word
ultimately means finally, so only the last letter of the word is kept

blocks.note: sure means certainly
the last letter of the word
a machine that is working is on

explanation.surface: A machine operator is certainly bored, with nothing working in the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons carry out operations, so in crosswords an operator often means a surgeon.

clue.text: Penny-pinching company secures great deal

indicators.note: secures means holds firmly, so the first word grips the second inside it

blocks.note: Co is the abbreviation for company
a heap is a great deal, as in heaps of time

explanation.surface: A cost-cutting firm lands a lucrative bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Great deal' suggests a bargain, which suits the stingy surface; it is simply a large amount.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheapo is informal for cheap or stingy, so it can describe penny-pinching ways.

clue.text: Children primarily linger outside small arcade

indicators.note: primarily means first of all, so only the opening letter is taken
outside means the verb's letters go round the next piece

blocks.note: the first letter of the word
to loiter is to linger
S is the abbreviation for small

explanation.surface: Kids mostly hang about in front of a little amusement arcade.
explanation.walkthrough: Arcade suggests slot machines; here it is a covered walkway of arches.
explanation.definitionFit: A cloister is a covered walk with an open arcade around a quadrangle in a monastery or college.

clue.text: Private person who's offended possibly rejecting society

indicators.note: rejecting means casting out, so that letter is removed from the word

blocks.note: to offend can mean to sin, so one who has offended is a sinner
S is the abbreviation for society

explanation.surface: A reclusive person, perhaps feeling hurt, shuns society.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Offended' suggests hurt feelings; here it means having done wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner thoughts or feelings are private ones, kept inside and not shared.

clue.text: Pasta spot close to Bari

indicators.note: close here is the end, so we keep only the final letter of the place name

blocks.note: a zit is a pimple or spot
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A pasta place located near the Italian city of Bari.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Close to' reads as near, but means the end of the city name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ziti is a type of tubular pasta from southern Italy.

clue.text: Belfries designed to incorporate a type of sculpture

indicators.note: designed means newly shaped, so the letters of the first word are rearranged
to incorporate means to take in, so the jumble absorbs the next letter

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Bell towers built to include carved decoration.
explanation.definitionFit: Bas-relief is low relief carving, where figures project only slightly from a flat background.

clue.text: Bottle used for pre-dinner vermouth

indicators.note: used for here means employed by the words that follow, whose letters supply the answer intact

blocks.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: A bottle that serves for an aperitif of vermouth before dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: Bottle is British slang for courage, as in 'lost his bottle'; the drinks setting disguises this.
explanation.definitionFit: Nerve and bottle both mean courage or daring in British slang.

clue.text: Peanuts, for example, are shelled inside fancy cast iron pot

indicators.note: shelled means stripped of the outer casing, so only the inner letter of the word is kept
fancy means elaborate or decorative, so these letters are rearranged into a new form
inside means placed within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: taken as written
the middle letter of the word

explanation.surface: Peanuts with their shells removed sit in an ornate iron cooking pot.
explanation.walkthrough: Peanuts looks like nuts to be shelled, but it is Charles Schulz's comic strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Peanuts, with Charlie Brown and Snoopy, is a famous example of a newspaper comic strip.
